message.content:
Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but they diverged from other carnivores early on. Their lineage split from the common ancestor of bears (Ursidae) around 20–25 million years ago during the Miocene epoch. Fossil evidence shows that the earliest members of the panda family were small, omnivorous mammals that lived in forested environments.

Over time, the giant panda evolved distinct traits such as a specialized wrist bone that acts like a pseudo‑thumb, allowing it to grasp bamboo stalks. This adaptation, along with a diet largely consisting of bamboo, helped the species survive in the changing climates of the Pleistocene. Despite being classified as a bear, the giant panda’s closest living relatives are actually the red panda (Ailurus fulgens), which shares some morphological features but belongs to its own separate family.
